question: Should Steward be a distinct product persona with its own canonical action universe, or a scoped level or role within Representative 2.2?

recoveryInference.statement: The repository treats the steward as the level-1 staff role under Representative 2.2. That reading rests on the evidence below and is not an institutional decision. It does not define a single steward action.

options.title: Distinct persona with an independent action universe
options.description: Steward has its own canonical, its own identifiers, its own workspace and its own authority statements, ratified separately from Representative 2.2.

consequences.workflows: Two parallel workflow definitions for the same case, assignment, evidence and correspondence steps. A change to a shared step must be made twice.
consequences.navigation: Seven steward destinations that duplicate seven representative destinations with narrower content.
consequences.authority: Risk that a second authority statement implies a second source of authority. Every steward action would still need to defer to the Representative 2.2 mandate.
consequences.continuity: A case moving between a steward and a representative changes persona definitions mid-flight and needs an explicit bridge.
consequences.delegatedAccess: Two delegation vocabularies to keep aligned.
consequences.testing: Duplicate acceptance suites and negative suites. Most steward tests restate representative tests.

tradeOffs: Clear product identity for a front-line user.
Highest chance of drift and duplicate ownership.
Implies, to a reader, a distinct office that no source names.

options.title: Scoped level within Representative 2.2 only
options.description: Steward is the level-1 capacity of Representative 2.2. No separate canonical, no separate workspace and no separate identifiers.

consequences.workflows: One workflow definition. Level 1 differences are filters.
consequences.navigation: One navigation set, narrowed by capability.
consequences.authority: One authority statement. The steward limit is expressed as what a level-1 capacity lacks.
consequences.continuity: No persona change when a case moves between levels.
consequences.testing: One acceptance suite with a level-1 profile. The steward-specific denials need a place to live.

tradeOffs: Least duplication and no implied office.
The front-line experience (queue, narrowed destinations, denials) has no named home.
Throws away the 55 steward contracts as a separate review unit and removes the only place that states the steward denials.

options.title: Scoped profile of Representative 2.2 with its own presentation profile and acceptance profile
options.description: Representative 2.2 is the single authority universe. Steward is a named profile of it: a workspace, a queue and a set of narrowing and denial contracts. Every steward contract names the Representative 2.2 parent it narrows and adds no power. The profile has its own acceptance and negative-test profile.

consequences.workflows: One workflow definition owned by Representative 2.2. The steward profile lists only the steps a steward takes and the steps a steward is denied.
consequences.navigation: Navigation is one capability-conditional set. The steward workspace is a presentation filter of it.
consequences.authority: Authority has one source. A steward contract can only restate or narrow a parent. A contract that adds a power is invalid.
consequences.continuity: A case moving between a steward and a supervising representative keeps one definition. The handoff is a normal Representative 2.2 handoff.
consequences.delegatedAccess: One delegation vocabulary, with the steward limits stated once in the profile.
consequences.testing: Shared acceptance suite plus a steward profile suite that proves the narrowing and the denials. Tenant and relationship tests run once for both.

tradeOffs: Keeps the front-line experience reviewable and the denials explicit.
Needs the shared-obligation mapping to stay accurate. The product owner must accept that Steward is not a separate institutional office.
The Steward package becomes dependent on the Representative 2.2 package, so the order of decision matters (DEC-PD-0C2-10).

recommendation.rationale: Every one of the 55 steward contracts names a Representative 2.2 counterpart, the recovered evidence places the steward at level 1 of the Representative 2.2 policy layer, and the proposed identity model already states that the workspace is a presentation choice that implies no office. The profile keeps what is useful about a distinct Steward experience and removes the duplicate authority statements.
recommendation.changesBaselineProposal: The proposed Steward baseline (DEC-PD-01 option 1) treats Steward as its own persona. Option C keeps the Steward contracts and the Steward package as a reviewable unit, and changes how the package is ratified and owned: the Representative 2.2 package is the authority universe and the Steward package is a profile of it.
